listings.name: Paris By Scooter
listings.content: All Vespa scooter rentals and Paris guided City tours include the collect and picked up from, your hotel in Paris.

listings.name: Eiffel Tower
listings.content: No other monument better symbolizes Paris.

listings.name: Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile
listings.content: The Arc de Triomphe exudes grandeur and offers a central view of the city.
listings.image: Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile in July 2011.jpg

listings.name: Champs-Élysées
listings.content: Widely regarded to be one of the most recognizable avenues in the world
listings.image: Champs-Élysées from the Arc de Triomphe.jpg

listings.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
listings.content: Impressive Gothic cathedral that was the inspiration for Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

listings.name: Sacré Coeur
listings.content: A church perched on top of the highest point in Paris. Behind the church is the artists' area, in front are spectacular views of the whole city.

listings.name: Opera Garnier
listings.content: Masterpiece of theatre architecture of the 19th century built by Charles Garnier and inaugurated in 1875 housing the Paris Opera since it was founded by Louis XIV.
listings.image: Paris Opera full frontal architecture, May 2009.jpg

listings.name: Catacombes de Paris
listings.content: Used to store the exhumed bones from the overflowing Paris cemetery. The bones of more than 6 million bodies lie here.

listings.name: Grande Arche de la Défense
listings.content: A modern office-building variant of the Arc de Triomphe.

listings.name: Panthéon
listings.content: Underneath, the final resting place for the great heroes of the French Republic including Voltaire, Victor Hugo, and Marie Skłodowska-Curie; above, a marvellous view of the city.

listings.name: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
listings.content: Unlike any cemetery in the world. Ornate grave stones, monuments set among tree lined lanes. See the graves of Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde, and Frédéric Chopin, among many others.

listings.name: Sainte-Chapelle
listings.content: Exquisite stained glass chapel. More beautiful interior than the gloomy Notre Dame Cathedral.

listings.name: The Louvre
listings.content: One of the finest museums in the world of art and culture. Home of the Mona Lisa and innumerable others. Enormous building and collection, plan at least two visits..

listings.name: Musée d'Orsay
listings.content: Incredible collection housed in a former railway station. Works by the great artists of the 19th century (1848-1914) including Monet's "Blue Water Lilies, Renoir's "Bal du moulin de la Galette", van Gogh's "Bedroom in Arles", Whistler's "The Artists Mother", etc.

listings.name: Rodin Museum
listings.content: Collection and archives dedicated to the sculptor Auguste Rodin, in a charming home with garden.

listings.name: Picasso Museum
listings.content: Contains the master's own collection.

listings.name: Musée Marmottan-Monet
listings.content: Over 300 paintings of Claude Monet. Also, the works of Berthe Morisot, Edgar Degas, Édouard Manet and Pierre-Auguste Renoir. "Impression Soleil Levant" by Monet is on display.

listings.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
listings.content: [Jardin des Tuileries] Houses "The Water Lilies" (or "Nymphéas") - a 360 degree depiction of Monet's flower garden at Giverny. Also, impressionist and post-Impressionist paintings by Cézanne, Matisse, Modigliani, Picasso, Renoir, Rousseau, Soutine, Sisley and others.

listings.name: Musée Delacroix
listings.content: Housed in the home of painter Eugène Delacroix.
listings.image: Delacroix Museum - The Studio from the Garden, Paris, sof2011.JPG

listings.name: Centre Georges Pompidou
listings.content: The museum of modern art. The building and adjoining Stravinsky Fountain are attractions in themselves. Closed for renovation until 2030.

listings.name: Les Invalides
listings.content: Very impressive museum of arms and armor from the Middle Ages to today. Also contains the tomb of Napoleon Bonaparte.

listings.name: Musée national du Moyen Âge
listings.content: A medieval museum exhibiting the five "The Lady and the Unicorn" tapestries, housed in a part Roman, part medieval building.

listings.name: Musée des Arts Décoratifs
listings.content: Showcasing eight centuries of French savoir-faire.

listings.name: Carnavalet
listings.content: Museum of Paris history; exhibitions are permanent and free. Renovated 2017–2021.

listings.name: Cité des sciences et de l’industrie - La Villette
listings.content: Science museum primarily for children.

listings.name: Mémorial de la Shoah
listings.content: Paris's Holocaust Memorial Museum, in the heart of the Marais on rue Geoffroy l'Asnier. Free Entry, weekly guided tours. Second Sunday of the month there is a free tour in English.

listings.name: Jacquemart-Andre Museum
listings.content: Private collection of French, Italian, and Dutch masterpieces in a typical 19th-century mansion.

listings.name: Guimet Museum
listings.content: One of the largest collections outside Asia of Southeast Asian, Indian, Afghan, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean art.

listings.name: French Open
listings.content: One of the four tennis Grand Slam tournaments. It is scheduled for two weeks from the last Sunday in May. The event, on clay courts, features the world’s top-ranked tennis players.

listings.name: Stade de France
listings.content: France's national stadium has a capacity of 81,338, and hosts concerts and various events. Soccer clubs sometimes play here when their home stadium is unavailable.

listings.name: Maison Européene de la Photographie
listings.content: Important center for contemporary photography with a large exposition area having three or four major expositions per year dedicated to contemporary photography. Housed in an updated hôtel particulier built in 1706. There is a large library, auditorium and café. Their archive houses over twenty thousand works of art. Admission is free every Wednesday from 17:00 to 20:00.

listings.name: Better Paris Photos
listings.content: Better Paris Photos offers instructional tours and workshops that combine hands-on learning of essential photographic techniques with guiding to, and commentary about, the most photogenic spots of Paris. Led by English-speaking photographers and instructors, these tours are open to all skill levels and interest.

listings.name: Le Foodist
listings.content: In the Latin Quarter, Le Foodist is an cooking school that offers French Cooking, Pastry and Baking Classes, Wine Tastings initiations, Food Tours and Hosted Gastronomic Dinners. Led by French Chefs, courses are made in English, small classes, with the ambition of teaching both the technique and the history of traditional French recipes.
listings.price: Prices range from €35 for a Wine Tasting Initiation to €180 for a Market class

listings.name: Le Cordon Bleu Paris
listings.content: Offering both long-term professional programs as well as short term hourly sessions, Le Cordon Bleu is one of the most famous culinary schools located in the heart of Paris. Le Cordon Bleu is considered to be the guardian of French culinary technique through its culinary programs that continue to preserve and pass on the mastery and appreciation of the culinary arts that have been the cornerstone of French gastronomy for over 500 years.

listings.name: La Cuisine Paris
listings.content: La Cuisine Paris is an English-friendly culinary school located in the heart of Paris, right on the Seine that offers expert teaching of the essential techniques of cuisine française. Led by an international group of English-speaking chefs all trained in classic French cooking, these classes are open to all skill levels and tastes.
listings.price: Prices range from €69 for a two-hour Macaron class to €160 for a 4 hour Market class
listings.address: 80 Quai de L'Hôtel de Ville, Paris 75004

listings.name: Palais des Glaces
listings.content: Grand palace with two theatres, the Palais des Glaces (Palace of Mirrors) features two shows, often two comics, simultaneously, and sometimes shows for children.

listings.name: Promenade Canal St. Martin
listings.content: Enjoy a leisurely stroll along the water's edge while viewing amazing sunsets over the canal. Linger over a coffee and tuck into a pastry while feeling that you are experiencing the true Paris.

listings.name: Porte Saint Denis
listings.content: A triumphal arch built in 1672 for Louis XIV, in the former city wall.

listings.name: Bang!
listings.content: Offers a selection of first class meats from all over the world (From American Angus and French Aubrac to Argentine Angus and Simmental from Bavaria), along with natural wines. The result is a friendly, warm space to meet friends, enjoy delicious food and converse against a soothing musical background of jazz and pop.

listings.name: Le Cambodge
listings.content: A small and charming restaurant with delicious Cambodian offerings. Order your selections by writing on the note card provided. Artistically inclined diners can see their orders memorialized as artwork on the walls.

listings.name: Chez Prune
listings.content: Primarily a drinking establishment, but serves food as well. The cheese plate, which is served with bread and fruit, is particularly good. Often quite crowded with locals. Waitstaff not necessarily proficient in English.

listings.name: Julien
listings.content: The original 1890 decor of this Parisian dining classic is a mix of Cuban mahogany and Art Nouveau paintings and fixtures - an atmospheric treat. The cuisine is mostly south-western French: lots of foie gras and the speciality, cassoulet d'oie (goose in white beans).
listings.price: Lunch €21, prix fixe €30, average plate €40, all cards taken.

listings.name: Restaurant La Strasbourgeoise
listings.content: One of the good "choucroutes" in Paris, with nice décor.

listings.name: Sésame
listings.content: A cute and comfortable little bistro with numerous vegetarian options, including an awesome vegi lasagne. The stove is warm and the staff are full of smiles.

listings.name: La Vigne Saint Laurent
listings.content: Tiny wine bar, good choice of classic country food (beautiful charcuterie) & good choice of reasonably priced wines.

listings.name: Khrishna Bhavan
listings.content: Serves excellent Indian vegetarian dishes from the southern state of Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka. First timers can consider trying the Thali, a combo platter consisting of steamed rice served with 5 different curries.

listings.name: Saravanaa Bhavan
listings.content: South Indian vegetarian chain restaurant.

listings.name: Bodhi Vegan
listings.content: Cheap and cheerful South-East Asian vegan fare run by a Vietnamese sect. The menu is pretty gigantic so you'll be very spoilt for choice!

listings.name: Tien Hiang
listings.content: East/South-East Asian vegetarian restaurant. The mock duck (canard laqué) is to die for.

listings.name: Jah Jah By Le Tricycle
listings.content: Hipstery vegan restaurant with a slight Caribbean twist.

listings.name: Daily Syrien Veggie
listings.content: Vegetarian Levantine cuisine.

listings.name: Baxo
listings.content: A lounge bar restaurant with a bobo environment and rich dishes. A new romantic lounge bar with a very nice patio.

listings.name: Le Verre Volé
listings.content: A part wine bar-part wine shop, an excellent address for nice, simple food & wines. You can take home a bottle you've sampled during meal if you wish!

listings.name: Au fût et à mesure
listings.content: A beer-bar coming with a new concept: one beer-pump on every table. Each table have its own distinct beer in the pump, so you have to meet people to taste other beers.

listings.name: Hotel de Maubeuge
listings.content: Simple and decent.

listings.name: Hotel Paradis
listings.content: The Hôtel Paradis, in the west part of the 10th near Gare du Nord and the Opéra Garnier has garnered mostly positive reviews over the years. Many travellers note that it seems to be a good value for money.

listings.name: Hotel Saint Quentin
listings.content: Quiet location in a little street, just in front of the Gare du Nord.

listings.name: Hôtel Vicq d'Azir
listings.content: This little cheapie is in the process of a renovation under its new management. Most of the rooms overlook a nice little courtyard with a tree.
listings.price: Rooms with a shower are €22.50/€28 singles/doubles or €18/€20 without a shower. Showers in the hall cost €3, so maybe go for the shower in the room

listings.name: Peace and Love Hostel
listings.content: Travellers who have a lot of hostel-staying experience mostly find the Peace and Love to be well within the high quality range for hostels. As usual in Paris the rooms are pretty small, the staff in general gets high marks, but the manager has been known to be crabby. Apparently the pub is good enough that there's some danger you might not go out. Must be between 18 and 35, and want to party to stay here. They suggest that if you want to sleep, this may not be the place for you.
listings.price: €17 for a dorm bed in the off season €21 during high season. Double rooms are €25

listings.name: Albert 1er Hotel
listings.content: The rooms are not too big but very clean and well-equipped. The staff are friendly and can send you an official reservation confirmation if you need it.

listings.name: Hôtel Paris Est Lafayette
listings.content: This 51-room hotel has modern furnishings decorated with warm colours. Staff are professional and efficient and there is 24-hr reception, as well as a tasty buffet breakfast each morning.

listings.name: Hotel à la Villa Saint Martin
listings.content: A 3-star hotel offering features such as free Wi-Fi , flat screen TV, fitness room.

listings.name: Quality Hotel Gare Du Nord
listings.content: Housed in a historic building dating back to 1868, the Quality Hotel includes in all its rooms modem plugs, Wi-Fi access, and tea & coffee makers.

listings.name: Le Citizen Hotel
listings.content: To an American, it will feel cramped, but it is well appointed and comfortable. Views of the canal locks are superb. Staff is extremely friendly and helpful, and daily breakfast is a magnificent start to the day.

listings.name: Cirque d'Hiver
listings.content: Mainly used as a concert hall and venue for fashion shows today, the Cirque d'Hiver was built in 1852, as the name would suggest, as a winter venue for circuses.
listings.image: P1020056 Paris XI Cirque d'Hiver reductwk.JPG

listings.name: Place de la Bastille
listings.image: P1160484 Paris IV-XI-XII place de la Bastille rwk.jpg

listings.name: Rue Nicolas-Appert
listings.content: This street is named in honor for Nicolas Appert, a French businessman who invented airtight food preservation. On January 7th, 2015, it was the site of the Charlie Hebdo terrorist attack, which resulted in the deaths of 12 people. A plaque in front of a former office building memorializes the victims of the satirical magazine's staff.

listings.name: Bataclan
listings.content: Attend a concert or have a drink at this popular café-concert music hall inaugurated in 1865 featuring brightly painted Chinese architecture. Always attracting a young crowd, the Bataclan has regained the splendor it once enjoyed and now books many emerging hip and rock acts. The café on the ground floor is outstanding, perhaps even better than in the old days. A memorial honoring those 90 persons killed in a terrorist attack on 13 Nov 2015 is across the street in a small park.

listings.name: Aux Comptoirs des Indes
listings.content: Indian.
listings.address: 50 rue de la Fontaine Au Roi

listings.name: Avé Maria
listings.content: Brazilian favela chic. The friendly folks who run this place have been hosting Brasilian dance nights at various venues around town. But don't just come in to check out the posters; stay a while for the fantastic vegetarian friendly South American and international cuisine at reasonable prices.

listings.name: Soya Cantine Bio
listings.content: A true organic, vegetarian restaurant, and a good one. The tiny bit of preciousness about the place is more than overwhelmed by the laid-back atmosphere and warm welcome. There are daily specials, but the couscous-soy will keep you coming back. Also check out the lunch buffet, but maybe not if you're counting calories because it's hard not to go up for thirds.

listings.name: Caffe Panem
listings.content: Pasta and bruschetta featured in this small family-run café that serves good and cheap coffee (90 cents for an espresso cup), croissants and great home made sweets such as tiramisu (standard and with chestnut purée). Evenings feature pasta and toasted bruschetta.

listings.name: Banoi
listings.content: Tiny Vietnamese restaurant featuring fresh authentic Vietnamese spring rolls, soup and sandwich banh-mi. Mix and match tapas. Vietnamese drinks and beer. They do a huge take-out and delivery business.

listings.name: Clown Bar
listings.content: The food served in this absolutely beautiful room is classic French. The decor is classic Circus, which makes sense since it's just two doors north of the building which has traditionally housed circuses passing through during the winter.
listings.price: The formule for lunch costs €13.50, while the dinner menu is €18.50. Ordering à la carte will cost you around €22

listings.name: Terra Rosse
listings.content: Authentic Italian pizzeria, restaurant and deli, The chef's offerings are very authentic and fresh. Top selection of pizza, antipasti, pasti and piatti caldi. Spanish and Italian deli meats are featured. The Italian staff are warm and helpful.

listings.name: Café Cannibale
listings.content: Very chic bar and café with DJ sets weekends; live music Friday and Saturday. Oysters direct from producers, seared octopus, chartouterie, steaks and fish. Wide selection of wine, beer, whiskies and cocktails. Happy Hour 16:00-20:00. Brunch Sundays.

listings.name: Le Bar à Soupes
listings.content: A large selection of different soups (including some vegetarian options). There are a few new ones each day. All served with your choice of an equally wide selection of breads and cheeses.

listings.name: Le Café des Anges
listings.content: Good variety of French café dishes with a few oriental offerings such as Bõ Bun. Quite a diverse menu. Some vegetarian, pasta and fish selections among the beef, pork and chicken dishes. Salads are fresh. Cocktails, beer, wine, whiskies, rums, cognac... the whole kitchen sink.

listings.name: Bistro Paul Bert
listings.content: A most classic Parisian bistro serving many first-time visitors to Paris and others who return. Appealing dishes are well plated and served, reliable and consistent from starter to dessert. This bistro is not a hidden gem as its well deserved reputation is widely known by tourists. Nevertheless if reservations are made in advance, seats are available and service remains excellent. The lunch menu is a remarkable value. Wine is diverse and served by the bottle or glass.

listings.name: Chez Justine
listings.content: Close to the centre of the Oberkampf nightlife zone, "Justine's place" functions as a restaurant & bar with mostly Italian food during the daytime early evening, but it's 22ː00-02ː00 which really makes the place. Most of the room is filled with big wooden plank tables which are just the thing for a lively conversation with friends, while the bar is comfy too, and attracts quite a crowd by the late evening. The decor is classic, understated, and classy.
listings.price: Draft beer at the bar is €5

listings.name: Grenier
listings.content: An excellent, but tiny dive bar with live bands upstairs in the hall some nights, but usually downstairs in the front window. This is a great place to hear Django Reinhardt-style jazz guitar playing (Jazz Manouche).
listings.price: A basic beer will set you back €2

listings.name: Nouveau Casino et Café Charbon
listings.content: The New Casino keeps rocking until dawn both in the bar downstairs and the medium-size dance hall upstairs, making it the favourite among young Parisians, especially after the other places in the neighbourhood have closed. The dance/concert hall features cutting-edge indie rock groups and cutting-edge electronica. The prices do reflect the hipness however.

listings.name: Le Perchoir
listings.content: Rooftop bar on the 6th and 7th floors of an old industrial building with a view of Paris from the four corners of the terrace. Expect a wait to enter on Friday or Saturday evenings. Once on the roof, there are unfinished wood, plants and colored cushions. Winter-mode, inside are bar and informal restaurant. See and be seen. The Snack Shack serves typical bar food. A wide selection of cocktails are available. DJ Sets.

listings.name: Entre Potes
listings.content: A good place to relax "among friends" as the name would suggest, thus making it a fairly representative Parisian bar, with notable cocktails.

listings.name: Les Marcheurs de Planete
listings.content: French wine bar with good prices and atmosphere and a friendly staff.

listings.name: Moonshiner
listings.content: Cool speakeasy bar with a secret entrance. Cross the small dining room of the pizzeria Da Vito and open the walk-in refrigerator door. You will enter into the bowels of an ancient American-style boiler room and bar. The interior welcomes brave visitors to a dim, classy and jazzy world. There you will find friendly steampunk bartenders making innovative cocktails. Try a cigar in the large Art Deco smokehouse... but shhhhh, don't tell anyone.

listings.name: Les Petits Crus
listings.content: Les Petits Crus is a wine bar specializing in a marriage between wine and cheese. Matched combinations can be chosen among reasonably priced wine and cheese by theme in 4 or 6 test tubes of quality wine of your choosing, accompanied with matching cheese, bread, salad and cold cuts if desired. All wine is organic.

listings.name: La Fée Verte
listings.content: La Fée Verte is an absinthe bar (and café) as it was known more than 100 years ago. Although no longer produced to be hallucinogenic, absinthe is an enjoyable alcoholic drink you prepare at your table. In the traditional French way, place a sugar cube on top of a specially designed slotted spoon over a small glass of absinthe. Next a large absinthe fountain with a crystal bowl of ice water and several small spouts is shared. Each person opens a valve to their spout and slowly drips the ice water onto the sugar cube until the cube is dissolved and the drink is diluted to their liking.

listings.name: Bluebird
listings.content: A real gin bar but they serve many other drinks, specialty cocktails included. Bar food is available but do not come for the food. This place is about cocktails.

listings.name: Auberge Internationale des Jeunes
listings.content: Rooms available for 2-4 persons. Price Includes are breakfast, shower, pillow, blanket and bed sheet for the mattress, access to the luggage room use of safe deposit box at the front desk. Age limit 30 years.

listings.name: Bastille Hostel
listings.content: This youth hostel features 29 rooms, some shared, some restricted to females only. Apartments available.

listings.name: Hôtel Voltaire République
listings.content: A few steps away from Republic Square. Local bakery, supermarket, laundry, and many other services are close to the hotel. All rooms are en suite, with TV and direct dial telephone. Wi-Fi is available in room.

listings.name: Au Royal Mad
listings.content: Budget hotel, with free toiletries, fridge, microwave, and TV in the rooms, and toilets & showers in the corridors. A stone's throw from Place Léon Blum (supermarket, bars, etc.) and Voltaire metro. Friendly staff. There is a room set aside for leaving luggage on the last day. Powerful, free wifi.
listings.price: €59.40 for a twin/double, including city tax

listings.name: Le Général Hôtel
listings.content: 3-star hotel. They've certainly put a certain amount of budget into graphic and interior design. Breakfast is not included.

listings.name: Grand Hotel Français
listings.content: The Grand Hotel Français Paris has been operated by the same family for over 100 years. They're quite proud of their hotel-operations lore handed down through the generations.

listings.name: Grand Hôtel Nouvel Opera
listings.content: 3-star hotel.

listings.name: Hôtel du Nord et de l'Est
listings.content: Found among a cluster of two-star hotels off of Place de la République, the North and East has been in the process lately of doing some renovation, bringing some of the rooms up to high three-star standards. Regardless of which type of room you book the place is quiet and cheerful and has Wi-Fi. It's a good value, and to top it off they often have vacancies when all of the hotels in more popular quarters are booked.

listings.name: Hotel Hor Les Lumiéres
listings.content: A budget hotel just a bit from République which offers a fitness centre, and free Wi-Fi, though "Le Marais" is a bit of a stretch.

listings.name: Hôtel Fabric
listings.content: Boutique hotel in an artistic neighborhood with 33 rooms is restyled in a 19th century textile factory that is both modern and characteristic of another era. The bold decor with brick walls and iron-works are comforting. Many services are available including fitness, hammam, massages, afternoon tea and concierge.

listings.name: Albert's Hotel
listings.content: Boutique hotel near many public transportation connections. Near lively neighborhoods but without the noise. Modernized bathrooms and bedrooms.

listings.name: Jardin Yitzhak Rabin
listings.content: Nestled in the centre of the Parc Bercy (below) is a lovely, and truly peaceful, garden with several waterworks and other high-quality landscape-art pieces. If you are one of the many people visiting the 12th on business it would be well worth an hour of your time between meetings and dinner to explore the mound, the fountain, and the bridges, and to watch children play in complete peace, much like the peace to which the garden's namesake dedicated his life.

listings.name: Bercy Village
listings.content: For a taste of the French countryside, a visit to Bercy Village brings to life the spirit of market shopping inside Paris.

listings.name: AccorHotels Arena
listings.content: An indoor sports arena that seats around 17,000 for sports and slightly over 20,000 for major concerts; formerly known as Palais des Omnisports de Paris-Bercy and Bercy Arena. Home to numerous concerts and major sporting events, most notably the Paris Masters tournament on the ATP World Tour in men's tennis.

listings.name: Opéra Bastille
listings.content: One of the truly great venues for the performing arts anywhere in the world, Paris' new opera house actually managed to inspire some neighborhood protest during its planning and construction. Pretty much everybody is a believer nowadays though. Check out the website for upcoming shows, it might even make sense to plan a trip to Paris around one.

listings.name: Promenade Plantée
listings.content: If you were a city planner in one of the great cities of our Earth and you discovered that a railroad right-of-way had been abandoned and would never be used again what might you do? Perhaps if you knew your stuff you'd convert it into a 4 mile long park, about half of which is elevated above street level on the old rail viaduct. This long narrow park pretty much allows the visitor to walk in carfree bliss from Place de Bastille to the Bois de Vincennes.

listings.name: Parc de Bercy
listings.content: Between the River Seine and the rail yards attached to Gare de Lyon and Gare de Bercy is a green space which would seem pretty huge if the 12th weren't also the home of the Bois de Vincennes. The park is a good place to hang out waiting for the line to form for sporting events and concerts at AccorHotels Arena.

listings.name: Bois de Vincennes
listings.content: There are many beautiful footpaths, a Buddhist Temple, and a lake with rowboats available for rental (about €10 as of 2009). The lake has many different kinds of birds, and islands accessible by footbridge.

listings.name: Picpus Cemetery
listings.content: A must for anyone interested in the history of the American Revolution. This small cemetery includes three mass graves from the French Revolution, plus a section that includes many of France's most noble families that lost members during the French Revolution and consequently have a continuing right to be buried there. In the farthest right hand corner is the tomb of General Lafayette, the friend and fellow soldier of George Washington. Beside him is his beloved wife plus other members of her family, the de Noailles, who were almost completely wiped out during the French Revolution because of their closeness to the Court. Since 1834 the American flag has apparently flown continuously over his grave, even during the German occupation of Paris during World War II. Well worthy of a visit.

listings.name: Château de Vincennes
listings.content: A former fortress and royal residence at the edge of the city, alongside the Bois de Vincennes. It was largely built between 1361 and 1369, and was a preferred residence, after the Palais de la Cité, of French kings in the 14th to 16th century. It is particularly known for its "donjon" or keep, a fortified central tower, the tallest in Europe, built in the 14th century, and for the chapel, Sainte-Chapelle de Vincennes, begun in 1379 but not completed until 1552, which is an exceptional example of Flamboyant Gothic architecture. Most of the building is now open to the public.

listings.name: Palais de la Porte Dorée
listings.content: Housed in an amazing Art Deco building, purpose-built for the 1931 Colonial Exhibition, featuring an elaborate frieze across the front facade that depicts the achievement of French overseas territories. It houses an Aquarium and an Immigration Museum. The aquarium can be seen in about an hour and is popular with families with small children.

listings.name: Cinema Museum
listings.content: Housed in modern building designed by Frank Gehry, contains a cinema showing French & international films, temporary exhibitions lasting about 6 months, Museum dedicated to the history of cinema. Exhibitions are fairly visual.
listings.price: Exhibition: Adult €12, Reduced €9.50, U18 €6: Museum Adult €10, Reduced&18-35 €7.50, U18 €5. Joint tickets available

listings.name: l'Ébauchoir
listings.content: A typical restaurant of the bo-bo (bourgeois - bohème) population of this district. Good traditional cooking with mid-range prices.

listings.name: Refuge
listings.content: This charming storefront bistro offers an adventurous take on traditional French cooking, and with a couple of good selections for vegetarians, including a €12 vegetarian menu. The indoor vineyard decor appeals for its artsy clutter; the only indications that the owner and chef is a former rugby star being the newspaper clipping on the wall and the almost hidden world championship medal behind the bar.

listings.name: Le Train Bleu
listings.content: Serves haute cuisine in amazing surroundings. Reservations strongly recommended

listings.name: Le Picotin
listings.content: An excellent find in a quiet back street. Good value food, with a selection wide enough to offer a good choice whilst allowing the chef to concentrate on perfecting a small number of dishes. Warm, friendly welcome and faultless service.

listings.name: Les Furieux
listings.content: An alternative bar at the end of the Rue de la Roquette, punk, rock, metal, goth.

listings.name: The Frog at Bercy Village
listings.content: Popular English brew-pub with a French twist. Open terrace at each end. Check the beer menu for current selection of beers brewed on the premises. Interesting range of snacks and more filling dishes.

listings.name: Hotel de France
listings.content: Located very close to Gare de Lyon and a short walk from Bastille, it is a decent budget hotel with single, double, triple and quadruple rooms. Convenient to visit Disneyland as well as to the sights of Paris.

listings.name: Hostel Blue Planet
listings.content: This hostel, within a block of the Gare de Lyon station, has bunk beds in shared rooms sleeping 4-6 people. Some rooms have showers and toilets. A basic breakfast of pastries and hot drinks is included in the price.
listings.price: €25 per bed. Towels and sheets extra.

listings.name: Hotel Le Quartier Bercy - Square
listings.content: Hotel Le Quartier Bercy Square, located in the 12th arrondissement, is right between Metro stations Dugommier and Daumesnil (Lines 6 and 8). It has easy access to Palais Omnisports at Bercy, Cours St. Emillon with its lively area of shops, restaurants, and bars, and train stations Gare de Bercy and Gare de Lyon. And with Line 14 at Bercy station just down the road, the rest of Paris is only minutes from you.

listings.name: AIJ Paris
listings.content: Some sites (including their own) says they are a youth-only hostel, but there do not enforce any age restrictions. Wifi and a small non-buffet continental breakfast is included. Each room has a sink, but the top sheet for each bunk is not included and will cost extra if you don't just want the blanket. No alcohol is allowed in the hostel. The hostel is 24 hr but the rooms close between 11:00-15:00 for cleaning.

listings.name: Grand Hôtel Doré
listings.content: Having opened its doors at the beginning of the 20th century The Grand Hotel Doré has been owned and operated by the same family ever since, giving the place plenty of character and quite a bit of charm. Guests tend to be a pretty even mix of business and pleasure travellers.

listings.name: Ibis Gare De Lyon Diderot
listings.content: This branch of the Ibis chain is a bit more comfortable than most, especially worthwhile if you have just arrived at Gare de Lyon. The website has current price information, and links to their 650 sister hotels across Europe. Breakfast (€10, until 10:00) is the pretty ordinary buffet fare.

listings.name: Hotel Palym
listings.content: This nice little hotel is around the right price and probably has the closest possible access to the Air France airport buses.

listings.name: Pullman Paris Bercy
listings.content: The former Sofitel was demoted to Pullman, but has since been afforded a thorough renovation (finished in autumn of 2013) to bring it up to current Pullman brand standards along with other Pullman hotels in Paris. Friendly and helpful staff.

listings.name: La Bibliothèque Nationale de France
listings.content: The national library preserves collections of historic documents of both French and international origin. It holds 5,000 Greek manuscripts. You can get a day pass to visit or choose to visit only the expositions the library hosts.
listings.image: France, Paris II Bibliothèque nationale de France, BnF, Site Richelieu, Salle Labrouste 1854-1875.jpg

listings.name: La Cité de la Mode et du Design
listings.content: Part gallery - part restaurant - part nightclub, La Cite (Les Docks) is a modern building that is instantly recognisable due to being draped on one side with a large neon green shell covering the stairwells and roof the building. Roughly translated in English as The City of Fashion and Design, this is a trendy spot at the weekends and is used for event like Paris Design Week. The restaurant in the building is open all year round.

listings.name: La Butte aux Cailles
listings.content: A little district within the district. Very charming little streets on a hill on the west end of the 13 district. Nice for lunching/dining activities. This is the place where the band "Mano Negra" was hanging around.

listings.name: Manufacture des Gobelins
listings.content: Once the dye works for royalty, it is now a museum.

listings.name: Stade Charléty
listings.content: The Stade Charlety is a massive multi-sport arena, hosting football (soccer), tennis, rugby and squash matches.

listings.name: Au Banquier
listings.content: Decor is minimalist, but the northern African cuisine of this place is delicious.

listings.name: Chez Gladines
listings.content: Big Basque salads and a lot of ambiance in this moderately low-budget restaurant. This place is almost always crowded on Saturday nights.

listings.name: Green Garden
listings.content: East Asian vegetarian

listings.name: Phở 14
listings.content: For Vietnamese soups, best known in the district.

listings.name: Sinorama
listings.content: One of many Chinese places in the outer part of the arrondissement.
listings.address: av de Choisy at rue de Tolbiac

listings.name: Sala Thaï
listings.content: Delicious Thai food.
listings.address: 13, rue des Frères d'Astier de la Vigerie

listings.name: Le Temps des Cerises
listings.content: If you are looking for quality French food and a large choice of good and affordable wine, this is the place to go. This is what we can call a restaurant populaire (as opposed to other posh and expensive places around) with a friendly staff, a very nice atmosphere, no way to reserve a table, just show up and the patron will find a place for you (arrive before 20:00 if you don't want to queue up, especially at weekends), turn off your mobile phone or you will be kicked out! The Boudin à la Normande (blood sausage) is a must and you can also get very decent goose liver and other French specialities such as Salade de Museau.

listings.name: Bateau Phare
listings.content: This little red lighthouse boat hosts dance and chill electronic music and other multimedia cultured events and has been one of the coolest spots around for some time. It was closed in or around 2018 but reopened in 2024 under a new name, "le Bateau Phare," that sounds just like the old one, "le Batofar." The dance floor is in the hold, a restaurant is above it, and the lounge on the upper deck. There is also a restaurant on the quai called "La Terrasse" that is open from May to October.

listings.name: La Dame de Canton
listings.content: Known for years as the Guinguette Pirate, this Chinese junk has been rechristened with her maiden name. The restaurant and bookings are still the same, with equal parts world music, chanson français and concerts for kids.

listings.name: Jack's
listings.content: On a very quiet street. Jean Genet died in this hotel in 1986.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Express Paris Place d'Italie
Mercure Gobelins
listings.address: 8 bis, av de la Soeur Rosalie

listings.name: Urban Bivouac
listings.content: 3-star hotel, 32 rooms.

listings.name: Les Catacombes de Paris
listings.content: One of the most eye-popping sights of Paris, the catacombs represent a network of labyrinthine tunnels, first excavated in the Roman period, that now house the remains of over 6 million burials removed here from the various overcrowded cemeteries and charnel houses all over Paris in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Well worth a visit: the atmosphere is suitably morbid and gloomy (without being too scary), the dark tunnels containing neatly stacked piles of skulls and long bones. There is a limit to the number of visitors allowed within the Catacombs at one time (200 persons). So, if you arrive just after opening, you must wait until someone exits, approximately 45–60 minutes, before anyone is admitted. Steep stairwell on the exit of the catacombs. Can be challenging for the elderly or the unfit. Tickets can be purchased online which allows you pick a date & time and to skip the long line.
listings.price: Adults (audioguide incl.): 31, Reduced rate (audioguide incl.): 25, Children (8 to 17 yo): 15; Adults (same day “last minute”): 15, Reduced rate (same day “last minute”): 13, Children (under 18): free; Audioguide: 5

listings.name: Cimetière de Montparnasse
listings.content: The burial place of existentialist philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre, feminist Simone de Beauvoir (both of whom lived nearby); musician Serge Gainsbourg; artist Man Ray; the poets Charles Baudelaire, Guy de Maupassant, Charles Sainte-Beuve, and Marguerite Duras; the founders of the Theatre of the Absurd Samuel Becket and Eugene Ionesco; the sculptors Constantin Brancusi and Ossip Zadkine; the composers Camille de Saint-Saens and César Franck; the actors Maria Montez and Jean Seberg; the French officer Alfred Dreyfus; the founder of the Larousse encyclopedia, Pierre Larousse; the industrialist André Citroen, and many others.

listings.name: Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
listings.content: The C.I.U.P. is a student quarter established in 1925, providing homes for about 10,000 students, scientists, and artists from 120 countries. It has 40 houses attributed to individual nations. The individual houses organise top quality cultural and political events. Among the most remarkable buildings are the Fondation Deutsch de la Meurthe, the Heinrich Heine House (Maison Heinrich Heine - Fondation de l'Allemagne), the Swedish Student House (Maison des Etudiants Suédois), and the Swiss Pavilion (Pavillon Suisse) which was built in 1933 on plans of Le Corbusier.

listings.name: Fondation Henri-Cartier-Bresson
listings.content: The foundation opened its doors in May 2003. It preserves Henri Cartier-Bresson and Martine Franck’s archives. Exhibition of photographs, paintings, sculptings, and illustrations.

listings.name: Lion of Belfort
listings.content: This is a bronze replica in smaller scale of a monument created by Bartholdi, the sculptor of the Statue of Liberty, in order to commemorate Denfert-Rochereau, who defended the city of Belfort in the Franco-Prussian war of 1870.
listings.image: P1150549 Paris XIV lion place Denfert-Rochereau rwk.jpg

listings.name: Observatoire
listings.content: The observatory was erected by Claude Perrault from 1667 to 1672 by order of Colbert. The building is oriented to the four cardinal directions. It is crossed in the centre by the Paris meridian (2° 20′ 14″ east of Greenwich). The observatory is not open to the public.
listings.address: 61, av de l'Observatoire, entrance: 77, av Denfert-Rochereau

listings.name: Parc Montsouris
listings.content: Considered one of the most colourful Parisian parks, a local favourite, the Parc Montsouris was opened in 1878, having been designed by Alphand for Baron Haussmann. A large man-made lake and waterfalls are surrounded by long stretches of gently sloping lawns. Bronze statues are to be found studding the grounds, amongst the 1,400 trees, including such exotic varieties as the giant sequoia and the ginkgo. The park is featured in the film Cléo de 5 à 7. It is popular among families (there are two playground areas for children) and students.

listings.name: Port-Royal Abbey
listings.content: Famous people who stayed here include Marie de Rohan, intriguer during the Fronde; Jeanne Baptiste d'Albert de Luynes, future mistress of a duke of Savoy; Marie Angélique de Fontanges, mistress of Louis XIV, died here giving birth to his child who also died. Today its main cloister (illustration) forms part of the modern Hôpital Cochin.

listings.name: Barrière d’Enfer
listings.content: The two pavilions were built in 1784 to 1787 by the French architect Claude-Nicolas Ledoux, who erected many similar toll houses at the entrances to the city.

listings.name: L'Amuse Bouche
listings.content: The cheese soufflés (soufflé au fromage) and Soufflé au Grand Marnier are highly recommended.

listings.name: L'Assiette
listings.content: Reservation recommended.

listings.name: Bistot du Dôme
listings.content: Seafood.

listings.name: La Cagouille
listings.price: Menu €38 including drinks, a la carte from €35-60

listings.name: La Cerisaie
listings.content: Reservation recommended.

listings.name: La Coupole
listings.content: The famous Art Deco brasserie, convenient for a quick meal before or after a train journey to or from Montparnasse station.

listings.name: Le Duc
listings.price: Set lunch €49, dinner a la carte €60-150

listings.name: Les Grillades de Buenos Aires
listings.content: Small and intimate Argentinian restaurant. Amazing steaks. Everything about the food is wonderful.

listings.name: Le Zeyer
listings.content: Famous Art Deco-style brasserie.

listings.name: Hotel Formula 1
listings.content: Very cheap private rooms, close enough to the metro to make it worth it. Rooms are very clean, and have TV, free Wi-Fi, and washbasin only. Shared showers and toilets. The showers are fine, but, there are no toilet-seats and no urinals (thus, the shared toilets get very nasty, very fast and people have to go back to their rooms to wash their hands in their washbasin), so the quality of the bathrooms may keep this hotel chain out of reach for serious germ-a-phobes. It is, nevertheless, cheaper for two people to stay here than just about any youth hostel in Paris. Nice and safe neighbourhood, too, with several supermarkets and kebab vendors for eats.
listings.address: 23, av de la Porte de Chatillon

listings.name: Voco Paris Montparnasse
listings.content: Contemporary style, central location, eco-friendly design, secure indoor parking. Wheelchair accessible rooms.

listings.name: Hotel Aiglon
listings.content: 20th-century filmmaker Luis Buñuel and sculptor Alberto Giacometti stayed in this hotel, which has good views, just next to the metro.

listings.name: L'hôtel du Lion
listings.content: An independent hotel on Place Denfert-Rochereau, near Montparnasse.

listings.name: Hotel Le M
listings.content: The hotel offers 59 fully renovated, comfortable and soundproofed rooms, in an elegant designer setting.

listings.name: Helzear Montparnasse
listings.content: Property with 14 suites and apartments. Each accommodation has a kitchenette and overlooks a quiet, paved interior courtyard. Configurations range from the duplex room (2 guests) to the 2-bedroom apartment and the deluxe suite sleeping up to 6, the latter featuring a private jacuzzi and sauna. 24-hour concierge, room service, luggage storage. No private parking, pets not allowed. Gaîté metro station (line 13) is a 7-minute walk away, Gare Montparnasse 10 minutes. Close to th

listings.name: Foyer Le Pont
listings.content: This is a budget-friendly place run by the German evangelical church in the Rhineland, it has a common room and fridge and you are allowed to bring you own drinks and food in, this is a quiet, simple place, in a good neighbourhood with a few restaurants, bakeries and supermarkets nearby.

listings.name: Marriott Rive Gauche
listings.content: A nice hotel and within two blocks of the St Jacques and Glaciere metro stations. Very friendly staff.

listings.name: Pullman Paris Montparnasse
listings.content: The gargantuan former Le Meridien was taken over by Accor's upscale brand Pullman and saw a complete renovation of its massive building housing 953 hotel rooms (the largest room count in Paris) on 26 floors. It has all the pros and cons of a huge business hotel, plus the added value of sweeping vistas from its rooms, due to its unusual height (116 metres) versus the Paris average.

listings.name: Tour Montparnasse
listings.content: If the queues at the Eiffel Tower are just too much for you and your time is limited, consider a trip up the Montparnasse Tower. This is an office building with an observation and shopping area on the 56th floor, where the elevators stop, and an open viewing area on the roof. Arguably the view is better than from the Eiffel Tower: you are not so high up so things are more visible, and you can see the Eiffel Tower!
listings.price: €11.50, with discounts, children under 7 are free of charge
listings.image: Remote view of the Tour Montparnasse & Eiffel Tower in 2005.jpg

listings.name: Île aux Cygnes
listings.content: One of the three islands on the river Seine
listings.image: Paris View from the Eiffel Tower third floor Ile aux Cygnes.jpg

listings.name: Square Béla Bartók
listings.content: A small park between two highrises on the Front de Seine featuring two interesting sculptures dedicated to the musician

listings.name: Statue de la Liberté
listings.content: Replica on the site where Bartholdi had his workshop

listings.name: St Christophe de Javel
listings.content: The first concrete church

listings.name: Pont de Bir-Hakeim
listings.content: Two-level bridge.

listings.name: Pont Mirabeau
listings.content: 19th-century bridge.

listings.name: Galerie Michèle Broutta
listings.content: Quality etchings, prints and collectors' books.

listings.name: Musée Bourdelle
listings.content: Sculptures by Antoine Bourdelle.
listings.image: Salle des plâtres du musée Bourdelle à Paris.JPG

listings.name: Musée Mendjisky
listings.content: Écoles de Paris housed in a Mallet Stevens Building.

listings.name: Musée Pasteur
listings.content: The Pasteur Museum is housed in the apartment where the great scientist spent the last 7 years of his life. Hardly touched since that time, the museum is full of personal memorabilia and scientific instruments. Pasteur is buried on the grounds in a flamboyant mosaic-decorated mausoleum. The museum was closed to individual visitors for security reasons after the 13th November 2015 Paris terrorist attacks.

listings.name: Jardin atlantique
listings.content: Suspended above the train tracks this garden is surprisingly calm and chilled-out.
listings.address: 1, place des Cinq Martyrs du Lycée Buffon

listings.name: Parc André Citroën
listings.content: The large park occupies the 14 ha formerly occupied by a Citroën factory. Several gardens have specific themes, including water games. On sunny weekends or vacation days many people chill out or jog there.

listings.name: Parc des Expositions
listings.content: Paris's international exhibition centre (the 4th largest in Europe) has millions of visitors annually.
listings.image: P1050990 Paris XV pte de Versailles entrée du parc des expositions rwk.JPG

listings.name: Aquaboulevard
listings.content: Biggest swimming pool and recreational center inside Paris.

listings.name: Ballon de Paris
listings.content: Get a unique bird's eye view of Paris on board an air-balloon, from an altitude of 150 m.

listings.name: Front de Seine
listings.content: Take a walk along the Front de Seine to appreciate the modern mixed use architecture between Bir-Hakeim bridge and Garigliano bridge, some of the buildings were designed by world renowned architects; The view is probably best from bridge Pont Mirabeau.

listings.name: Maison de la culture du Japon
listings.content: The location hosts several expositions, a library and a concert hall.

listings.name: Tour Montparnasse, Top deck
listings.content: Panoramic view of Paris from the 56th floor.

listings.name: le Cordon Bleu
listings.content: Le Cordon Bleu is the world's largest hospitality education institution, with over 50 schools on five continents serving 20,000 students annually. Its education focus is on Hospitality Management, Culinary Arts, and Gastronomy. Offering Diplomas in Cuisine, Pastry and Bakery for the aspiring chef as well as short courses, workshops, and guest chefs demonstrations for gourmet enthusiasts. Julia Child, who famously popularized the art of French cuisine in America, graduated from this school in the 1940s, as portrayed in the movie Julie & Julia by Merryl Streep.

listings.name: Choux d'enfer
listings.content: Street food + haute pâtisserie française = sweet food in a designer "kiosk".
listings.address: Intersection rue Jean Rey and quai Branly

listings.name: Café Beaugrenelle
listings.content: Brasserie on lively Place Charles Michels

listings.name: Le Café du Commerce
listings.content: Authentic French food and ambience. (Be sure to go to number 51 rue du Commerce, as there is another place nearby with a similar name.)

listings.name: La Plage Parisienne
listings.content: Along the River, rather pleasant. They also offer cocktails at their bar.

listings.name: Le Volant
listings.content: The Basque restaurant excels in meat. If you are lucky the soup of the day is the "soupe au marron". There is a possibility to get a 3-course evening menu including entrée, plat and dessert. The home-made "mousse au chocolat" is really big. Also the bistro is generous on the sides: Usually one gets "purée", rice and polenta. Inside the restaurant, the former tricot of the famous French football player Zinedine Zidane is on display. As the small place fills rapidly, reservation is recommended.

listings.name: Au Roi du café
listings.content: Belle-Epoque decor, true bisto spirit

listings.name: Bermuda Onion
listings.content: Eat or drink. View of the river even better in the evening.
listings.address: Centre commercial Beaugrenelle, Ilôt Verseau - 3rd floor, 7 rue Linois, 75015

listings.name: Eclectic
listings.content: Brasserie fashion. Decor Tom Dixon

listings.name: Le Baribal
listings.content: 40-year-old neighborhood bistro run by Louisette and her partner George. Traditional simple fare.

listings.name: Frame Brasserie
listings.content: Californian-style restaurant : a new take on the traditional Parisian brasserie.

listings.name: Afaria
listings.content: This Basque restaurant mainly serves meat or some fancy tapas on the bar.

listings.name: Le Beurre Noisette
listings.content: The restaurant of Thierry Bianqui offers interesting food all year long. Remember to reserve in advance for this cosy place. The menu are written on chalk boards and they can arrange custom demands for vegetarians. The desserts are recommended.

listings.name: Le Ciel de Paris
listings.content: 360° view.

listings.name: Restaurant Benkay
listings.content: Japanese cuisine. Great views.
listings.address: Hotel Novotel Front de Seine Grenelle, 61 quai de Grenelle

listings.name: Celtic Corner Pub
listings.content: A nice little Irish pub with charming service and fair price. Sports men from the nearby Gymnase "Croix Nivert" like to hang out here for a beer or two.

listings.name: Crocodile Vert
listings.content: The small hidden Cuban bar is a bit away from rue de Vaugirard. It is quite popular for the salsa music on the weekends. At later times you'll recognise it by the number of people standing outside.

listings.name: Le square café
listings.content: In spring time sun is shining on the outdoor terrace. It is a nice spot for a tea with soft background music.

listings.name: Le César Palace Paris
listings.content: Diner and show - Parisian cabaret show and dancing.

listings.name: Aloha Youth Hostel
listings.content: No membership card required.

listings.name: Campanile Paris XV - Tour Eiffel
listings.content: English & Spanish spoken at reception.

listings.name: Hotel Mirabeau Eiffel
listings.content: Though it is off centered, It is new, clean and somewhat affordable

listings.name: Hôtel Oceania Paris Porte de Versailles
Mercure Paris Centre Tour Eiffel
listings.content: A relatively large mid-range hotel very close to the Eiffel Tower, in a nice, quiet and green area of Grenelle. Despite the closeness, only about a quarter of the rooms, designated as such and commanding higher rates, feature a view of the tower itself. All of the rooms and common spaces have been renovated and feature modern decor inspired by the tower and the metro. The rooms are very functional and feature operable windows, but the amounts of plastic and the violet theme may not provide for a romantic Parisian experience.

listings.name: Mercure Paris Tour Eiffel Grenelle
listings.content: Not to be confused with the other Mercure, this one is not far away but in quite a different setting, facing the busy Boulevard Grenelle and the overground Metro 6 line. Neither as quiet nor as modern or comfortable as the other Mercure. On balance it is one of the cheaper hotels in its class close to the core tourist centre of Paris.

listings.name: Novotel Paris Tour Eiffel
listings.content: The largest Novotel in the world was built as a Japanese hotel Nikko, and retains many interesting design elements of the former, like the capsule-style windows, and the Japanese restaurant Benkay. It is by now not ageing that well though and awaits the long-overdue renovation.

listings.name: Novotel Paris Gare Montparnasse
listings.content: Located in a quiet corner of Montparnasse, and if you don't mind a 10-min walk to the Metro, this is a nice and relatively new hotel. Easy access from the Montparnasse-Bienvenüe Metro: just take the stairs all the way up to the train platforms, exit on Boulevard de Vaugirard, take a left and follow the street up to the hotel. There is a Velib' City Bike Rental park just outside the hotel.

listings.name: Esteem Tour Eiffel
listings.content: 4-star hotel with 29 air-conditioned rooms in the Beaugrenelle district, close to the Eiffel Tower. Spread over 4 floors with elevator access. Buffet breakfast, concierge service, multilingual staff.

listings.name: Hotel Sublim Eiffel
listings.content: Funky decorated rooms located within 15min walk from the Tour Eiffel.

listings.name: Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel
listings.content: The former Hilton was taken over by Accor's upscale business hotel brand Pullman and underwent extensive renovation to its rooms and public spaces. It continues to offer close-up views of the Eiffel Tower from the balconies of its relatively spacious for Paris Deluxe (32 m²) and Superior (26 m²) rooms, while the Classic rooms (26 m²) face the courtyard.
listings.price: Room-only rates starting from €205, breakfast is €25 per person

listings.name: Palais de Chaillot
listings.content: Great perspective on the Eiffel Tower and Left Bank from Place du Trocadéro in between the two buildings of the palais. Former location of the Palais du Trocadéro. It accommodates three museums, an aquarium, and the Theatre Nationale du Chaillot.

listings.name: Musée Marmottan
listings.content: This charming museum is owned by the French Académie des Beaux-Arts. Its main collection areas, the result of several large donations, include: First Empire art and furnishings; illuminated manuscripts; and Impressionist art, including the largest Monet collection in the world and works by Renoir, Manet, Morisot, Caillebotte and Gauguin.
listings.price: €12; children under 18 and students under 25 €8.50; children under 7 and people with disabilities free

listings.name: Musée en Herbe
listings.content: With a teaching style based on fun and humour, the Musée en Herbe offers classes and games about art especially designed for children. Observation, imagination and identification games permit kids to discover the works of art and objects shown, at their own pace. The exhibits are all hands-on so kids can have a free reign in the museum, and if that's not enough there are workshops as well.
listings.price: €4 for the exhibitions, €8 for the workshops, but add €2.70 for entrance to the garden. Some discounts are available

listings.name: Palais de Tokyo
listings.content: The Palais de Tokyo is Paris's largest specialist contemporary art exhibition venue, owned and operated by the national government. The building dates to 1937 and also includes the Museum of Modern Art of the City of Paris.

listings.name: Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris
listings.content: The east wing of the Palais de Tokyo holds the modern art collection of the city of Paris, dating roughly from World War I to date (the older part of the collection is at the Petit Palais in the 8th), including around 10,000 works.
listings.price: Free, temporary exhibitions have various charges
listings.image: Musée d'Art moderne de la Ville de Paris.jpg

listings.name: Musée Dapper
listings.content: This small museum hosts high quality African art exhibitions. It also features an interesting bookshop and cafe.
listings.price: Adults €6, concessional rate €4, free on the last Wednesday of each month

listings.name: Fondation Louis Vuitton
listings.content: 20th- and 21st-century art in a building designed by Frank Gehry

listings.name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent
listings.image: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Avenue Marceau Paris 16 - Vue1.jpg

listings.name: Musée Nationale de la Marine
listings.content: Reconstructed in 2023, the Paris branch of the National Maritime Museum, one of the three museums in the Palais du Chaillot, cannot accommodate any full-size ships, but has a wide range of smaller artifacts, artworks and models, covering both the Navy and commercial shipping.
listings.price: €12 at ticket office, €11 online. Free to under eighteens

listings.name: Musée de l'Homme
listings.content: The Museum of Mankind, accommodated in the Palais du Chaillot, is an anthropological museum covering the history of mankind and human societies.

listings.name: Cité de l'architecture & du patrimoine
listings.content: The City of Architecture and Heritage, accommodated in the Palais du Chaillot, is a museum and gallery of French architecture. The centrepiece is the spectacular Hall of Casts, a collection of full-size plaster casts of facades, towers, doorways and windows of great buildings from all over France. Architecture of the late 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries is represented by additional galleries of models and images.
listings.image: Cite de l'architecture et du patrimoine.jpg

listings.name: Guimet Museum
listings.content: Has one of the largest collections abroad of Asian art.

listings.name: Jardin d'Acclimatation
listings.content: The northwest corner of the Bois de Boulogne is occupied by the oldest operating amusement park in the world, the Jardin d'Acclimatation, which is mainly known for offering a wide range of amusements which are appropriate even for very small children. They have miniature roller-coasters for children as small as three years, and the usual range of pony rides etc.

listings.name: Jardins du Trocadéro
listings.content: Tourists cross this park with the large fountain on the way to the Place du Trocadéro viewpoint to the Eiffel Tower.

listings.name: Immeuble Molitor
listings.content: An 8-storey block of flats, built in 1932–1934.

listings.name: Castel Béranger
listings.content: Castel Béranger is an apartment building that was the first entirely art nouveau building in Paris, insulted at the time as "Castel Derangé". Its richly decorated facade won a city competition in 1898. It contains 36 apartments, all of which are still privately owned and not open to the public.

listings.name: Hôtel Guimard
listings.content: Guimard's own home, built in 1909-12. It is less decorated than Castel Béranger, but still beautifully shaped. Privately owned and not open to the public.

listings.name: Hôtel Mezzara
listings.content: House designed by Guimard in 1910-1 for Paul Mezzara, the owner and designer of a lace and embroidery manufacturer. As of October 2025, under renovation to become a museum dedicated to Guimard, expected to open in 2027-8.

listings.name: Bois de Boulogne
listings.content: A park along the western edge of the 16ème arrondissement of Paris, near the suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt. The Bois de Boulogne has an area of 8.45, which is 2.5 times larger than Central Park in New York, and 3.3 times larger than Hyde Park in London. At night time, the area welcomes a different scene, and becomes one of Paris' most prominent red-light districts.

listings.name: Swim at Piscine Molitor
listings.content: A stunning classical swimming pool complex. The pool is known for its Art Deco designs and the popular introduction of the bikini by Louis Réard on 5 July 1946. The character Pi Patel in the novel/movie Life of Pi was named after this pool. Nowadays it houses a 5-star hotel as well. Access for non-hotel guests is very pricey — you must book a spa package for €230.

listings.name: French Open
listings.content: The second of each year's four Grand Slam tennis tournaments is held over two weeks in late May and early June at Stade Roland Garros in the Bois de Boulogne. The venue is open for tours year-round whenever tournaments are not scheduled, and the French Tennis Federation operates its national museum of the sport, the Tenniseum, at the site.

listings.name: Paris Saint-Germain
listings.content: PSG play soccer in the top-tier Ligue 1. They often win it and qualify for European tournaments. Parc des Princes stadium (capacity 48,000) is south side of Bois de Boulogne. The club name derives from St-Germain-en-Laye 20 km west, not the city centre district of Saint-Germain-des-Prés.
listings.address: Parc des Princes, 24 Rue du Commandant Guilbaud

listings.name: Stade Français
listings.content: Rugby club in the Top 14, and a perennial title contender. Stade's traditional home ground of Stade Jean-Bouin, across the street from Parc des Princes, reopened in 2013 after a major renovation. Ticket information is available online in English.

listings.name: Horse racing
listings.content: Some of the world's best thoroughbred racing can be seen at two venues in the Bois de Boulogne.

listings.name: Hippodrome de Longchamp
listings.content: Used exclusively for flat racing, the venue hosts many of France's top races, including the internationally famous Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe on the first weekend in October.

listings.name: Hippodrome d'Auteuil
listings.content: Used exclusively for steeplechase racing, and hosts many top-quality races in that discipline. Its flagship event is the Grand Steeple-Chase de Paris.

listings.name: Carette
listings.content: This Pâtisserie and Salon de thé also has great food. The salads are amazing, and there are delicious cakes for dessert.

listings.name: La Gare Chaussée De La Muette
Le Malakoff
listings.content: Just take the menu of the day

listings.name: Le Coq
listings.content: A hip and trendy modern brasserie where the 16th arrondissement's posh population meets

listings.name: Café Brassac
listings.content: Very nice cafe with good lunch and dinner. Lots of people go their for business lunch

listings.name: L'Astrance
listings.content: 3 Michelin stars. Considered one of the best restaurants of Paris. Do not go there, if you are hungry and want to get full.

listings.name: Café de l'Homme
listings.content: Get a fantastic view of the Eiffel Tower from this restaurant-tearoom opposite the Champ de Mars. Just next to the Musee de l'Homme, there certainly are worse spots to grab a drink or two. Bad service towards tourists according to online reviews.

listings.name: Le Hameau de Passy
listings.content: Clean, quiet and good value hotel located in the centre of the Passy area

listings.name: Hotel Eiffel Kennedy
listings.content: Small three star hotel (33 rooms).

listings.name: Hôtel Gavarni
listings.content: In the heart of the Passy village and its fashion boutiques. It's the first independent hotel in Paris to have been awarded the European Ecolabel. Fully air-conditioned, free WiFi.

listings.name: Mon Hotel
listings.content: A boutique hotel in the vicinity of Place d'Etoile

listings.name: Hotel Longchamp Elysées
listings.content: 3-star boutique hotel.

listings.name: Helzear Champs-Élysées
listings.content: Property with 27 suites and apartments located at 49 avenue Marceau, in the 16th arrondissement, close to the Champs-Élysées and the Arc de Triomphe. Accommodations spread over 6 floors with elevator access in a Haussmann-style building, each featuring a kitchenette and air conditioning. Configurations range from the Tiny room (11 sqm, 2 guests) to the 2-bedroom apartment sleeping up to 6, with several suites offering a private terrace. 24-hour concierge, room service, luggage storage. George V metro station (line 1) is a 3-minute walk away, Charles de Gaulle - Étoile (lines 1, 2, 6, RER A) 10 minutes. Close to the Palais de Tokyo, the Musée d'Art Moderne, and the Fondation Yves Saint Laurent.

listings.name: Hotel Keppler
listings.content: In the entertainment district with 34 guestrooms and 5 suites. A winter garden and bar is available within the hotel.

listings.name: Peninsula Paris
listings.content: This meticulous hotel, known before the Second World War as the Hotel Majestic, has 200 rooms including 24 suites in this classic 19th-century Haussman building.

listings.name: Renaissance Paris Le Parc Trocadero
listings.content: A quiet small hotel with a courtyard north of metro Victor Hugo. Wired internet at rooms.

listings.name: Hotel Molitor - MGallery Collection
listings.content: The Piscine Molitor swimming pool complex, featured prominently in the book and film The Life of Pi, has been pretty much dismantled and rebuilt after many years of decay, becoming reborn triumphantly in 2014 as a luxury hotel, a part of the MGallery Collection.

listings.name: Parc Clichy Batignolles Martin Luther King
listings.content: The largest park in the 17th, completed in 2020. It has various installations for kids and sports. It's a good spot to see flowering trees during spring.

listings.name: Château des Ternes
listings.content: The last remains of a castle dating from the 16th century

listings.name: Le Palais des Congrès de Paris
listings.content: A large convention center and concert venue.

listings.name: Brasserie Wepler
listings.content: Excellent service, open late, seafood specialities. It is closed for renovations.

listings.name: Restaurant Brigitte
listings.content: Finely prepared french cuisine served in a fancy bistrot environment. One of the notable point of this restaurant is their large collection of Chartreuse liquors.

listings.name: A Jean Bart
listings.content: A typical Parisian brasserie, with all the classic food options. Croques monsieur are available at the counter.

listings.name: Le Bar Belge
listings.content: Opened in 1954 as Paris was finally recovering from the occupation, the Bar Belge serves dozens of different Belgian beers, ales, and lambics in a locals-dominated, but very friendly room. They also have Vlaams Frites, the original "french" fries. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Les Caves Populaires
listings.content: A major bobo hangout, this one specialises in wine as opposed to the more beer-oriented Lush.

listings.name: Lush
listings.content: Grungy atmosphere and a well thought out selection of beers and tunes have made this a popular space with the bobo crowd. There's not much in the way of furniture, so it's standing room only when the place gets hopping. Of course that means you can fit more hipsters per square metre.

listings.name: Hôtel Acacias Etoile
listings.content: A clean, well-run hotel in the side streets near Place Charles de Gaulle. The staff is friendly, the rooms aren't large, but they are immaculate.

listings.name: Mercure Paris Arc de Triomphe Etoile
listings.content: Modern rooms featuring frosted glass and stiff curtain dividers between sleeping areas and bathrooms, which may not be to everybody's liking. The most expensive rooms enjoy terraces with views over the 17th all the way to La Défense.

listings.name: Novotel Paris 17 Porte d'Asnières
listings.content: A typical Novotel in a faraway corner of the 17th, not really close to anything nor particularly conveniently located.

listings.name: Hotel L'Eldorado
listings.content: A former maison de rendez-vous, a home to the kept women of the 19th century bourgeois. Now a 4-star hotel.

listings.name: Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile
listings.content: The tallest hotel in Paris is the lone skyscraper in the northwest of Paris, adjacent to the Palais du Congres. It enjoys an unobstructed line of sight towards the Eiffel Tower from the rooms facing it and its top-floor bar. After Hyatt took over the property, it is being gradually updated, but still not entirely up to the best Hyatt worldwide standards.

listings.name: Le Méridien Paris Arc de Triomphe
listings.content: The first Le Meridien in the world, built in 1972 to cater for Air France passengers arriving on the newly-acquired widebody jets. Behind the distinctive 1970s facade are updated rooms and common areas with contemporary design and facilities. The hotel faces the Palais du Congres and caters mostly for business travellers. This is the largest hotel by room count in Paris, with 1,025 rooms of various types. The less expensive Classic and Deluxe rooms have more dated decor, the Urban and Executive rooms have been thoroughly updated to 21st century standards.

listings.name: Renaissance Paris Arc de Triomphe
listings.content: The Renaissance is a thoroughly modern property with floor-to-ceiling windows in the posh Avenue Wagram, just a short walk from Place de l'Étoile. The building was designed by the same Christian de Portzamparc who gave the Palais du Congres its current appearance.

listings.name: Sacré-Cœur
listings.content: This wedding cake-white church rises visibly above the north part of Paris. The striking building, with its towers and white onion dome (83 m high), was built between 1875-1914 on the birthplace of La Commune, officially as an act of penitence for the sins committed during the civil war in which thousands of Communards were executed, as well as for the previous bloodshed of the 1870 Franco-Prussian war. A number of prominent businessmen put up the money, and a dizzying combination of architects worked to put together the mock Romano-Byzantine extravaganza. Consecration followed in 1919. The view over Paris from the dome and from the square before it (200 m above sea level) is unsurpassed, apart from that enjoyed at the Eiffel Tower (50 km on a clear day). For the athletic traveller there are stairs from several directions to the top of the hill; otherwise there is also a funicular which runs every few minutes during the daytime from Place St. Pierre. Follow the signs that say "Funiculaire De Montmartre". Beware that the guards don't like it if they catch you taking pictures inside and will even yell "No photo!" and chase you down if they see you with a camera. Be warned: along the lower steps leading up to church, groups of mostly young African men gather and reach toward you with a small string, offering to loop it round your finger. In case it happens, pull back your hand, brush them off and move on. They might claim that "This is for the church." In case your feel that things go sideways, raise your voice to get people's attention and ask them call the police.

listings.name: Cimetière de Montmartre
listings.content: There are a number of famous occupants, but the real reason to visit this cemetery is to see the ornate tombstones, sculptures, and other sometimes macabre, sometimes touching memorials Parisians have left here for their dead.

listings.name: Artists' Square
listings.content: Numerous artists paint portraits of tourists and also sell their paintings.
listings.image: Paris Montmartre Place du Tertre dsc07247.jpg

listings.name: Place Pigalle
listings.content: The sleaze of boulevard de Clichy between place Pigalle and place Blanche can provide a moment of distraction. Be warned if you are male it is better to do this in the company of a female fellow traveller, as the clubs often send the girls outside to attempt to physically drag passing men off of the street. These strip clubs are big ripoffs. They tempt you with a free drink for €10 entry; once in the girl who starts dancing orders a couple of drinks (Red Bull) and then before you realise you are presented with a bill ranging from €500-700. They have these big bouncers who threaten/manhandle you till you arrive at some settlement with them. The whole of Pigalle is a rip off, best avoided. The police know about these places but nothing is done.

listings.name: Moulin de la Galette
listings.content: Built in 1717, the windmill is now part of a restaurant of the same name, and is easily visible from the street.

listings.name: Moulin Blute-Fin
listings.content: The windmill is within fenced private property, and may be difficult to see from the street, especially if there are leaves on the nearby trees. It is near the more visible Moulin de la Galette.

listings.name: Espace Dali
listings.content: A fantastic and undeservedly little-known collection of the great surrealist artist's often overlooked sculptural works. Those travellers seeking a more authentic experience should be warned that the majority of works here are reproductions, and that this "museum" is more appropriately considered as a for-profit, tourist-oriented homage to the artist rather than a carefully curated collection of original work. To find it, head up to Sacré Cœur and stand facing it and take a left. Keep your eye out for small Dali signs.
listings.price: Admission €11 adults, €7 seniors 60+, €6 children and students under 26, free for children under 8

listings.name: Musée de Montmartre
listings.content: The museum is located in a 17th century house with a garden, and features the history and culture of Montmartre. Several famous artists had lived in the house including Renoir.

listings.name: "I love you" wall
listings.content: Wall with the words for "I love you" written in many languages.
listings.image: Le mur des je t'aime, Paris 26 August 2013.jpg

listings.name: Abbesses métro station
listings.content: The station's beautiful entrance (circa 1900) is one of only two remaining glass-covered "dragonfly" entrances designed by Hector Guimard (1867–1942). It was featured in the film Le Fabuleux destin d'Amélie Poulain. While the entrance is genuine, this is not an authentic location for it, as the station was originally constructed by an independent Metro company that did not use Guimard's entrances.

listings.name: Villa Léandre
listings.content: Villa Léandre is a short residential street where the houses have small front gardens giving the street an English look.

listings.name: Vigne du Clos Montmartre
listings.content: Montmartre has a small vineyard which can be seen through a chain-linked fence. One of its products (vin Clos Montmartre) can be purchased at the nearby Musée de Montmartre.

listings.name: Buste de Dalida
listings.content: Dalida was a chanteuse and actrice who sold 170 million albums and singles worldwide. The bust faces the attractive Rue de l'Abreuvoir. The breast area of her bronze bust has a bleached colour possibly due attention given by overly enthusiastic admirers.

listings.name: Le Passe-Muraille
listings.content: The sculpture of a man walking through a store wall like a ghost was inspired by a novel by Marcel Aymé about a civil servant who takes revenge on people who humiliated him after he discovered he could pass through walls.

listings.name: Le Moulin Rouge
listings.content: With two shows a night, this turn-of-the-20th century burlesque palace offers a big production choreographed dance show interspersed with comedians, jugglers, and magicians. The show is more than bilingual, actually playing up the U.S. 4th infantry's involvement in the libération for the sake of the large number of Americans in the audience. If you want to spend more you can have dinner there. Is the Moulin Rouge a tourist trap? Well... it was meant to be one in the first place, so the experience is genuine.
listings.price: It's not cheap: the 21:00 show costs €95 and the 23:00 show costs €89

listings.name: Cooking with Class
listings.content: Hands on French cooking classes in a relaxed atmosphere with an experienced French chef. 4 hours of fun, including market visit, cheese and wine tasting, 5 minutes from the Sacre Coeur in the heart of Montmartre.

listings.name: Môm'artre
listings.content: An arts centre intended primarily for kids (Môme means kid) the Môm'artre features workshops for kids and adults, hosted by neighborhood artists.

listings.name: Nawab
listings.content: This Indian and Pakistani restaurant is usually packed especially for lunch so be sure to call ahead and reserve a table. One of the reasons is that if you ask them to spice it up "like in Pakistan" they actually will.

listings.name: Le Surcouf
listings.content: Very ordinary non-touristy cafe run by family from the Maghreb.
