"French" food is pricey for what you get, but the couscous dishes are huge, cheap and delicious with a home-cooked feel to them. There's a dog hanging around the bar, very friendly beast, but avoid if allergic or easily scared.

listings.name: La Travesia
listings.content: Inexpensive but excellent Lebanese food. Vegetarian friendly. Just down the steps from the Sacre Coeur.

listings.name: Au Grain de Folie
listings.content: A one-woman operation with some mixed reviews, but apparently when she gets it right it's just about the best dining experience you'll ever have. Booking a day ahead is suggested.

listings.name: Le Buffet
listings.content: Tasty, homey French food in a family-run restaurant. Lunch menu is around €12 (can be had until 20ː00).

listings.name: Cafe des Deux Moulins
listings.content: A popular destination for those who love the film Le fabuleaux destin d'Amelie Poulain, yet some locals still come here. Interior preserves the movie set. Great for lunch.

listings.name: La Petaudiere
listings.content: Piano bar. Tasty food, nice ambience, and excellent good piano music (prepare some coins for the pianist).

listings.name: Le Refuge des Fondues
listings.content: Fondue restaurant for young people: menu for €17, including wine served in a baby bottle, appetizers, the fondue itself (cheese or meat), and dessert.

listings.name: La Taverne de Montmartre
listings.content: Small restaurant with a nice rustic decoration, just below the artist's square, place du Tertre. Relaxing place, not overloaded with tourists. Excellent fondue offered for €17 per person (Oct 2008), including a salami salad for starters.

listings.name: Markotte
listings.content: Organic sandwiches, salads and soups

listings.name: Le Basilic
listings.content: Very nice atmosphere and service. Great food, and good selection of wines.

listings.name: Au Progres
listings.content: Small bar in an old place.

listings.name: La Boule Noire
listings.content: A small venue which is decorated to resemble a 1920s speakeasy, which has hosted a range of musicians from local singers to major arena acts.

listings.name: Le Divan du Monde
listings.content: A fairly major venue for indi-rock, hip-hop, and other concerts. The prices are usually pretty good and the size of the venue and decor are great.

listings.name: Olympic Café
listings.content: Run as part of the Laboratoire Multi-culturel populaire the Olympic Café is one of the few places in Paris where you can reliably find avant-garde jazz, making it at least spiritually a descendant of the club where the Art Ensemble of Chicago were resident for 5 years or so in the early 1970s. In addition to jazz they book music from around the world, especially Africa and the Caribbean.

listings.name: Truc Café
listings.content: A classic French wine bistro filled with young trendy singles.

listings.name: Auberge de jeunesse Hi Paris Yves Robert
listings.content: IYHA youth hostel close to Gare du Nord & Gare de l’Est.

listings.name: Hôtel Bonséjour
listings.content: The hands-down winner in value for price at the low-end, the Bonséjour offers 34 Spartan, but immaculately clean rooms on 5 floors. Internet terminals and Wi-Fi available.
listings.price: Singles with no shower start at €33, or €66 with a shower. The shared shower downstairs costs €2

listings.name: Plug-Inn Hostel
listings.content: A small and inexpensive, but clean and well-located hostel. Free Wi-Fi, but the signal is weak in the rooms. Free breakfast.

listings.name: Hotel Sofia
listings.content: The rooms are simple, but look comfortable enough, and the street seems to be a quiet one for Montmartre. As a little bonus, all of the rooms have a shower. Free Wi-Fi.
listings.price: Singles start at €50, plus €3 if you want to watch TV, but you're in Paris, so why would you do that? Breakfast is €7

listings.name: Adagio Paris Montmartre
listings.content: This "Aparthotel" opens out onto a peaceful interior garden.

listings.name: Hotel des Arts
listings.content: Consistently getting the highest possible reviews in its price-range, this well-located hotel was entirely renovated since 2000. The rooms upstairs are said to have fantastic views, but at least one reviewer online warns of being bumped because of over-booking.

listings.name: Le Chat Noir
listings.content: This former cabaret and now boutique hotel combines the bohemian spirit of Montmartre with a modern and cool aesthetic.

listings.name: Hotel Damremont
listings.content: Close to Butte Montmartre in a quiet residential quarter.

listings.name: Hotel Eden Montmartre
listings.content: A basic, but nice two-star, the Eden is on the far side of the hill of Montmartre from the city, and that can be a good thing if you are looking for a more authentic view of Parisian life.

listings.name: Ibis Montmartre
listings.content: The rooms are a little small, but this offering of the Ibis chain is up to the usual high standard of cleanliness and service. Of course if you need a toothbrush you can find it in the vending machine downstairs. Reception is staffed around the clock for late arrivals.

listings.name: Timhotel Montmartre
listings.content: This cute, very well kept two-star is closer to a three-star in quality and price, it's just that the rooms are on the small side. Some of the rooms in the upper floors have fantastic views of the city.

listings.name: Kube Hotel
listings.content: Stylish and atmospheric, the Kube Hotel exudes a high tech and luxurious decor. All the rooms come equipped with individual air conditioning, digital door opening, multi-function computer (DVD, CD, TV screen), cable TV, ADSL Internet, strongbox, mini bar, and fully equipped bathroom. As its name might suggest, the rooms feature some sort of cubism design and even the bedside tables look like ice cubes. Go out at night in your very own hotel, with a DJ spinning in the bar nightly, as well as being Paris's first-ever ice bar.

listings.name: Terrass Hotel
listings.content: Excellent four star hotel in Montmartre with 98 rooms, en suite baths, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, good restaurant, business facilities. The rooftop restaurant with fantastic views of Paris is open May-Sep.

listings.name: Canal de l'Ourcq
listings.content: Built in the 19th century by Napoléon to provide Parisians with drinking water. On sunny days, tourists can cruise along the canal or kayak its length.
listings.address: 13, quai de la Loire Bassin de la Villette
listings.image: Canal de l'Ourcq pres de Vignely P1050588.JPG

listings.name: Cité des Enfants
listings.content: An interactive science museum for children with the aim of arousing their curiosity, answering the questions they ask, and providing quality time for exchanges with parents or teachers.
listings.address: Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie, 30, av Corentin-Cariou

listings.name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
listings.content: Opened in 1986 and continuously upgraded, substantially damaged by a 2015 structural fire. This attraction drew over 7 million visitors a year who come to explore the world of science, technology and future possibilities. Includes the Louis Lumière 3D cinema.

listings.name: Cité de la Musique
listings.content: Music museum that focuses on the culture, the listening and the learning of music. With headsets, visitors can enjoy listening and learning about the history of music. Part of Philharmonie de Paris.

listings.name: Buttes-Chaumont Park
listings.content: Popular city escape for nature lovers and walkers who can spend hours wandering around this lush green paradise. Biggest, most hilly, and least touristy park in Paris, here you still find a real Parisian atmosphere, far from the crowds at the city's centre (it still is crowded in summer during weekends as many Parisians come to sunbathe on the grass). Climb on top of the hill and overlook the north of Paris with the Montmartre hill right in front of you. The park has an almost enchanted feel, with its waterfall (water is pumped from the nearby canal Saint Martin), stream, lake and its steep cliff, topped with a "temple" which can only be reached via a suspension bridge. A true oasis indeed

listings.name: Cafezoïde
listings.content: A café for kids, the Cafezoïde a fully weekly calendar of events for kids from 2-16 years old. An English-language sing-along happens on Thursday afternoons at 16ː00.

listings.name: Au Boeuf Couronné
listings.content: Charming and laid-back, this restaurant has a somewhat old fashioned decor (think hard leather chairs, etc). As of May 2024, the food and the service are reported as no longer top-quality.

listings.name: Café de la Musique
listings.content: Its varied selection of music is what draws the crowds here en masse, at any given night you're likely to hear soulful jazz tunes, or a hip DJ spinning robotic techno. Under chef Alain Podou's watch, the food here is sophisticated, yet light, think lobster-studded risotto and brochettes of shrimp with spinach. Highly recommended.

listings.name: Rosa Bonheur
listings.content: This buvette near the south edge of the Parc des Buttes-Chaumont offers a range of tapas and drinks in a charming relaxed atmosphere. Hang out on a sunny day and watch the kids run around and play.

listings.name: La Cascade
listings.content: Quiet bar that serves its beers cold and has an extensive wine list.

listings.name: Péniche Anako
listings.content: Canal d'Ourcq barge, this one specializing in shows celebrating cultures from around the world. On the Quai de Loire side.

listings.name: Péniche Antipode
listings.content: A boat on the Canal d'Ourcq which is now a restaurant & music venue. On the quai de Seine side.

listings.name: Paname Brewing Company Tap House
listings.content: Tap house with 16 beers on tap and restaurant. Great views across along the Ourcq. Pizzas, burgers and salads available.

listings.name: St Christopher’s Inns Paris Hostel
listings.content: A brand new purpose built hostel in Paris opened in 2008.

listings.name: Hotel Crimee
listings.content: Close to the Metro, the hotel boasts a quick and easy connection to downtown Paris.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Express Canal d'Ourq
listings.content: A quite unusually interesting Holiday Inn Express, sharing the building facing the Bassin de La Villette with St. Christopher's Inn. Some rooms have terraces with views of the bassin.

listings.name: ibis Paris la Villette Cite des Sciences
listings.content: Hotel with view of the Junction of the Canals Ourcq & St Denis from rooms at the front of the hotel.

places.title: Bastille
places.blurb: The Bastille was a medieval fortress in Paris, known as the Bastille Saint-Antoine.

places.title: Arènes de Lutèce
places.blurb: The Arènes de Lutèce are among the most important ancient Roman remains in Paris, together with the Thermes de Cluny.

places.title: Café Procope
places.blurb: The Café Procope, also known as Le Procope, on the Rue de l'Ancienne Comédie, is a café in the 6th arrondissement of Paris.

places.title: Bourse de commerce
places.blurb: The Bourse de commerce is a building in Paris, originally used as a place to negotiate the trade of grain and other commodities, and later to provide services to businesses by the Paris Chamber of Commerce during the…

places.title: Boulevard Saint-Germain
places.blurb: The Boulevard Saint-Germain is a major street in Paris on the Rive Gauche of the Seine.

places.title: Boulevard du Temple
places.blurb: The Boulevard du Temple, formerly nicknamed the "Boulevard du Crime", is a thoroughfare in Paris that separates the 3rd arrondissement from the 11th.

places.title: Café de la Régence
places.blurb: The Café de la Régence (French pronunciation: [kafe d la ʁeʒɑ̃s]) in Paris was an important European centre of chess in the 18th and 19th centuries.

places.title: Boulevard Saint-Michel
places.blurb: The Boulevard Saint-Michel is one of the two major streets in the Latin Quarter of Paris, France, the other being the Boulevard Saint-Germain.

places.title: Abbey of Saint Genevieve
places.blurb: The Abbey of Saint Genevieve was a monastery in Paris.

places.title: 59 Rivoli
places.blurb: 59 Rivoli is an art gallery in Paris, France.

places.title: Archbishop's Palace of Paris
places.blurb: The Archbishop's Palace of Paris was the residence of the Archbishop of Paris, located just south of the Notre-Dame de Paris.

places.title: Agoudas Hakehilos Synagogue
places.blurb: The Agoudas Hakehilos Synagogue is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 10 rue Pavée, in Le Marais quarter, in the IVe arrondissement of Paris, France.

places.title: Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal
places.blurb: The Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal in Paris has been part of the Bibliothèque nationale de France since 1934.

places.title: Café de la Gare
places.blurb: The Café de la Gare is a dinner theater located at 41, rue du Temple in the 4th arrondissement of Paris, at the western end of the historic Marais district.
